name: Service registration
description: Where a host object becomes a name the guest can reach, and who may change what stands behind that name.

scenarios.title: A bound path answers with what was bound to it
given: a registry with nothing bound
scenarios.when: an object is bound at a multi-segment path
scenarios.then: that path resolves to the object

scenarios.title: Binding chains
given: a registry with nothing bound
scenarios.when: an object is bound at a path
scenarios.then: the bind answers the registry it was called on

scenarios.title: A single segment is a whole path
given: a registry with nothing bound
scenarios.when: an object is bound at a single-segment path
scenarios.then: that path resolves to the object

scenarios.title: A path is what it spells, not what it is written as
given: a registry holding one path bound as a Symbol and another as a String
scenarios.when: each is resolved by its String form
scenarios.then: each answers the object bound under it

scenarios.title: A Service is whatever answers the call
given: a registry with nothing bound
scenarios.when: a class, an instance and a module are each bound at their own path
scenarios.then: all three paths resolve to the objects bound at them

scenarios.title: A single-segment path reaches the guest with no namespace
given: a Sandbox with a Service bound at a single-segment path
scenarios.when: guest code names that path as a top-level constant and calls it

scenarios.title: Each prefix segment becomes a guest module
given: a Sandbox with a Service bound at a three-segment path
scenarios.when: guest code walks the module chain the prefix spells and calls the leaf

scenarios.title: Leaves under one namespace stand beside each other
given: a Sandbox with two Services bound under the same prefix
scenarios.when: guest code calls each leaf by its full path
scenarios.then: each answers from its own Service

scenarios.title: A namespace is the whole prefix, not its first segment
given: a Sandbox with Services bound so that two share a two-segment prefix and two more meet only at their root segment
scenarios.when: guest code calls each leaf by its full path
scenarios.then: each answers from its own Service

scenarios.title: Unrelated paths do not see each other
given: a registry holding Services at two unrelated paths
scenarios.when: each path is resolved

scenarios.title: Siblings under one prefix do not collide
given: a registry with a Service bound under a prefix
scenarios.when: a second Service is bound under the same prefix at a different leaf
scenarios.then: both paths resolve to their own objects

scenarios.title: A path is bound once
given: a registry with a Service bound at a path
scenarios.when: the same path is bound again

scenarios.title: A name is a Service or a grouping, never both
given: a registry with a Service bound at a single-segment path
scenarios.when: a path extending it is bound

scenarios.title: A grouping cannot become a Service either
given: a registry with a Service bound at a two-segment path
scenarios.when: that path's prefix is bound

scenarios.title: A refused bind changes nothing
given: a registry with a Service bound at a path
a bind refused for colliding with it
scenarios.when: the original path is resolved
scenarios.then: it answers the object bound first

scenarios.title: An unfilled path is a path that resolves to nothing
given: an invocation whose registry declares a path with no object
scenarios.when: that path is resolved

scenarios.title: A declared but unfilled path fails closed
given: a Sandbox declaring a Service path with no object
scenarios.when: guest code calls that path and leaves the failure unrescued

scenarios.title: The sentinel is the declaration, spelled out
given: a Sandbox binding `Kobako::Unresolved` at a path explicitly
scenarios.when: guest code calls that path and leaves the failure unrescued

scenarios.title: A declared name and an unknown one are told apart
given: a Sandbox declaring one Service path with no object
scenarios.when: guest code names a constant that was never declared

scenarios.title: The guest may carry on past an unfilled path
given: a Sandbox declaring a Service path with no object
scenarios.when: guest code calls that path inside a rescue and returns a value

scenarios.title: An override outranks the binding it shadows
given: an invocation whose registry holds an object at a path
an override bound at that path for this invocation
scenarios.when: the path is resolved

scenarios.title: An override is how an unfilled path gets filled
given: an invocation whose registry declares a path with no object
an override bound at that path for this invocation
scenarios.when: the path is resolved

scenarios.title: An override cannot introduce a name
given: an invocation whose registry declares one path
scenarios.when: an override is bound at a path the registry never declared

scenarios.title: What the override fills is what the guest reaches
given: a Sandbox declaring a Service path with no object
scenarios.when: guest code calls that path during an invocation whose block filled it
scenarios.then: the filled object's answer comes back

scenarios.title: The override block serves the entrypoint verb too
given: a Sandbox declaring a Service path with no object and carrying a preloaded entrypoint that calls it
scenarios.when: the entrypoint runs during an invocation whose block filled that path
scenarios.then: the filled object's answer comes back

scenarios.title: An override shadows a bound object as readily as an empty path
given: a Sandbox with an object bound at a path
scenarios.when: guest code calls that path during an invocation whose block bound another object there

scenarios.title: An override is spent with its invocation
given: a Sandbox with an object bound at a path
an earlier invocation that overrode it
scenarios.when: a later invocation with no block calls that path

scenarios.title: A block that fills nothing changes nothing
given: a Sandbox declaring a Service path with no object
scenarios.when: guest code calls that path during an invocation whose block left it unfilled

scenarios.title: A Context is spent when its block returns
given: a Context captured out of a completed invocation's block
scenarios.when: an override is bound through it afterward

text: A binding is observable twice over: on the host, where a path resolves to an
object, and in the guest, where the same path has become a constant to name.
Both are witnessed, because a path that resolves correctly on the host and
materializes under the wrong module reaches nobody.
The collision scenarios are three refusals and one survival. The survival is
separate because a registry that raises and half-applies the bind would pass
A path declared without an object and a name never declared at all fail
differently, and that difference is the point: one is a capability the host
has reserved, the other is nothing. The override scenarios then cover who may
change what stands behind a declared name, and for how long — never for
longer than one invocation, and never for a name that was not already there.
A malformed path segment and a bind after the seal both raise, so they belong
to the error taxonomy and are specified there. The declared path set that
every invocation ships belongs to the invocation, not to registration.
